pr_title: fix(debug controller): highlight selectors in iframe
pr_body:
Closes https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/issues/33146. We were only sending the selector to the main frame, so it didn't reach the `iframe`. The fix is to send it to all frames, and use a heuristic to figure out the intended one.

I placed this heuristic inside the injected script. We could probably also put it inside the server part, not sure which is preferable.

issue_context.title: [Feature]: locators in iframes not getting highlighted in Chromium or any browser
issue_context.body:
### 🚀 Feature Request

I would like to see locators within multiple iframes getting highlighted in Chromium or any browser, so I can troubleshoot my iframe locators easily from Visual Studio Code.

Currently, the following default playwrights locators are highlighted in Chromium.
```
page.getByText('foo');
page.getByRole('button', { name: 'foo' });
etc...
```

For locator within one iframe, sometimes I see them getting highlighted in Chromium, sometimes not.
```
page.frameLocator('iframe').getByText('foo');
```

And for locators within two or more iframes, I have never seen them getting highlighted in Chromium.
```
page.frameLocator('iframe1').frameLocator('iframe2').getByText('foo');
page.frameLocator('iframe1').frameLocator('iframe2').frameLocator('iframe3').getByText('foo');
```

In order for me to troubleshoot these iframe locators, I have to use playwright's highlight method, but I need to run my test every time when I work on a new locator.

```
let fooLocator = page.frameLocator('iframe1').frameLocator('iframe2').getByText('foo');
await fooLocator .highlight();
```

With that said, if I can see these locators from Chromium without running my test every time for a new locator, it will greatly increase my efficiency.

### Example

_No response_

### Motivation

This will help troubleshoot iframe locators much faster.
comments: @qk5 Could you please be more specific in how do you expect locators to be highlighted? Are you doing it through the VSCode extension? What exactly do you do? Any specific page this happens on? The more details you provide, the better the chances we'll be able to help.

review_comments: i'm assuming that `page.frames()` returns all frames recursively, not just the top level ones
Note: you can add `selector` property to the result of `resolveFrameForSelector()`, it is already available there.

I don't see how. `frameChunks` contains parsed selectors, not strings. And we can't use the `selectorString` that's passed into `evaluateHandle`, because it points to frames not to elements in frames. I'll go ahead without this change, let me know how this would work and i'm happy to open a follow-up PR.
Let's also check that `frameLocator().frameLocator().getByText()` does not highlight anything.
